doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Not planning a career; thinking about money and ownership
summary: Harris says he never planned a diversified career, loves music, and learned about real estate and investing while keeping music separate from money.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well that’s really interesting because was it a conscious decision, let’s say most young musicians go through struggles trying to make a living. Did you say to yourself I need to do other things as well as play mallet instruments if I want to create a career for myself?

No I didn’t. I don’t think I ever went through that type of clarity when I was very, very young. I mean I just love music. I mean I still — I’m more energized, I work harder now than I ever have in my entire life and I have so much joy and passion for music. And I think that authenticity was infectious ever since I was a little kid in sixth grade playing an instrument I just led with so much happiness and also wanting to share and connect with people in vulnerability. And I think we’re at a point in our society where that’s something that’s hard to come by and people perceive vulnerability. And then when I think about making a living, I remember years ago, this is I was already touring but I remember having a conversation with a group of musicians and I was saying how well if you want to think about money there’s nothing wrong with that, but out of all the options in the world right now you’re choosing jazz if it’s about money? I’m not so sure that’s the best decision. And I reached a point where I said okay, well I didn’t have kids at the time but I want to have kids one day and I want to be able to provide the best that I can for my children and I need to think more about money so I started to read some books about real estate and investing and other things. So when I think about money I start to think about the concept of ownership, creating something that can be a commodity that can be sold. I never think about money as it relates to my music or the vibraphone. I like to keep it separate. Whether if I were a billionaire I would still practice just as much. I’m not motivated by money. For me.
